articles.title: Dianna Russini marks return to social media by taking advantage of NFL Trade Deadline with first post since Mike Vrabel scandal
articles.standfirst: Russini hadn't posted on her X account since April, and she's now promoting her new show.
articles.summary: Russini hadn't posted on her X account since April, and she's now promoting her new show.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of the Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel scandal, it was clear that the New England Patriots head coach was somewhat in the clear; at least professionally. Russini is the one who suffered the most, as she was fired from The Athletic and her journalistic career was in jeopardy.

But over the past couple of weeks, rumors began circulating that Russini was working on a big comeback. That was confirmed this week, as " The Russini Report " has been announced. It's a new weekly show featuring Russini that will cover NFL topics. It's set to premier on Wednesday, November 12 on BetUS TV .

Now that she's back in the media fold, Russini is taking advantage of her reporting connections and the timely NFL Trade Deadline to resurrect her social media career . In her first post on X since April 2 , Russini dropped some " What I'm Hearing " insider knowledge.

Dianna Russini returns to X with first post since April 2

Russini reports that the Minnesota Vikings are calling around the league for available quarterbacks. They even tried to poach Mac Jones from the San Francisco 49ers , but they're asking for too much at the moment. She also echoed Adam Schefter 's report that Kirk Cousins is still Minnesota's top option.

She also made sure to promote her new show in a follow-up post. The premiere episode will feature special guests Bill Parcells , Damon Amendolara , and Spike Eskin .

Fans didn't exactly take too kindly to Russini's first X post in seven months. They won't let her live down the Vrabel scandal.

articles.title: “$12,000 in rent and now rats?”: Shilo Sanders slams life in New York following disgusting encounters in restaurants
articles.standfirst: Deion Sanders' son has discovered another drawback to his potential move to the Big Apple
articles.summary: Deion Sanders' son has discovered another drawback to his potential move to the Big Apple
articles.body:
S hilo Sanders is finding that life in New York might not be quite as appealing as he initially imagined.

The former Colorado Buffaloes safety has been enjoying his time in the city, but a series of unpleasant encounters has left him questioning whether he could actually make it his home.

His latest complaint has nothing to do with basketball, football or the city's famously expensive apartments.

Instead, Sanders says rats have become an increasingly uncomfortable part of his experience, including an encounter inside a restaurant that reportedly sent him rushing outside.

In an Instagram Reel posted on November 9, the son of Colorado head coach Deion Sanders explained why the situation was becoming difficult to tolerate.

“I love New York. I’ve had a great time out here, but every place I go into, it’s rats, bro,” Shilo said. “I can’t do this. I promise you, I’ve seen three rats out here since I’ve been here. I can’t live like that, bro.”

The video then captured another moment after Sanders apparently left a restaurant because he spotted a rat inside. Someone subsequently informed him that the animal had been caught, prompting a relieved response.

“Oh, you got it? Oh, all right, they got it, bro,” Shilo said. “I had to run out of here. I can’t do this, bro.”

His reaction was another indication that the city might not be winning him over, particularly after his earlier concerns about the cost of finding somewhere comfortable to live.

The $12,000 apartment problem is still hanging over his decision

Sanders had previously discussed the possibility of relocating to New York during a house-hunting conversation in Florida. He initially appeared enthusiastic about exploring the market, even suggesting that he would film the search.

“I’m actually going to go out there and do a house hunt video there ’cause I’m trying to look in New York. Should I move there?” he asked.

However, the reality of the city's property prices quickly became a concern. In an earlier video, Sanders questioned how much living space renters actually receive for the money they spend.

“My biggest thing about New York, bro, is the square footage for the price,” Shilo said. “I don’t know who normalized the real estate market in New York, but it’s outrageous, bro.”

He suggested that even a monthly budget of $12,000 might not secure the type of apartment he wanted. That figure is far above the city's typical rental prices, but it highlights the level of luxury Sanders appears to be considering.

The wider market offers little encouragement. Realtor.com's October 27 rental report found that New York City's median asking rent reached $3,785 in the third quarter of 2026, a 4.5% increase compared with the same period last year. Manhattan was considerably more expensive, with a median of $5,375, while Brooklyn reached $4,197.

Sanders has also explored properties in Florida, including expensive rentals in Miami and Fort Lauderdale.

One downtown Miami property reportedly caught his attention because of its river views, but its $14,000 monthly price was too much for him. His brother, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, even offered to help with a down payment on a house.

New York's rat problem, meanwhile, has become a familiar part of the city's reputation. There has been some progress: the Department of Sanitation reported that 311 rat-sighting complaints fell from 25,230 between December 2023 and November 2024 to 20,025 during the following 12 months, a 20.6% decrease. The city has attributed the improvement in part to requirements for buildings and businesses to store rubbish in sealed containers.

Still, Sanders ' personal experience appears to have made a strong impression.

“I was gonna go house hunting, all that stuff, but I don’t know, bro. This ain’t my type of place,” Shilo concluded in the reel.

For now, the former college football player has not ruled out spending more time in New York, but finding an apartment he likes may not be enough.

After the expensive property search and the restaurant encounters, Sanders has another question to answer: whether the lifestyle is worth the price.
